title: Pipe Forecast
summary: Predict what short dplyr pipelines return before R runs them.
hints: Work through a pipeline one step at a time, writing down the small table after each step.
`pull(col)` hands back one column as a plain vector, so R prints it with `[1]`.
Each verb only sees the columns that are still there after the step before.

quiz.explain: Ada (7), Cai (9) and Dee (5) all score above 4; only Ben (3) is dropped.

quiz.prompt: What order do the names come out in?
quiz.explain: `desc()` sorts largest first: 9, 7, 5, 3. `pull(name)` then hands back the names in that order.

quiz.prompt: What does the new column hold?
quiz.explain: `mutate()` works row by row: each score doubled. R pads numbers to the same width when it prints them, so the 6 gets an extra space.

quiz.prompt: Team means: what does R print?
quiz.explain: `group_by(team)` splits the rows into team A (7, 9) and team B (3, 5); `summarise()` gives one row per team: 8 and 4.

choices: It prints Ada, Cai and Dee
It prints all four rows, because `score` was dropped
An error: `score` isn't in the data any more
It prints an empty data frame
quiz.explain: `select()` kept only `name` and `team`, so by the time `filter()` runs there is no `score` column. **Order matters in a pipeline**: filter first, then select.
